IDE auto-load: VSCode/Cursor/Claude/Gemini spawns scripting host referencing Miasma persistence config AIExploitation Medium
Catches the on-open execution path: Code.exe/Cursor.exe/claude.exe/gemini.exe spawning node/powershell/cmd/bun/python where the command line or parent context contains one of the persistence file paths from the StepSecurity table (.vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen, .claude/setup.mjs SessionStart, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc on-load, etc.). This is the post-clone execution moment after UC1's file landed. Rationale: Each (IDE parent, scripting child, persistence-path cmdline marker) tuple is lifted directly from Table 1 of the article. The runOn:folderOpen / SessionStart triggers genuinely fire on project open in the legit case, so the cmdline path marker is what raises this above noise - without it the detection is unworkable, with it the detection only fires when the IDE is invoking one of the seven Miasma/Hades persistence files specifically. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-miasma-and-hades-worms-target-bioinformatics-and-mcp-developers-via-malicious • https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/hades-campaign-pypi-shai-hulud • https://www.scworld.com/news/mini-shai-hulud-hades-variant-affects-23-pypi-package-versions
ATT&CKT1546 T1059 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-authored .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen running legitimate lint/build steps
  • Devcontainer postCreateCommand spawning node setup scripts from .vscode/
  • Claude Code SessionStart hook installed by the developer themselves for legit local automation
  • Cursor rules pointing to a user-authored setup.mdc with project-bootstrap logic
  • Repo template that ships a benign .github/setup.js for org-mandated git hooks
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "devcontainer.exe")
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("eslint","prettier","tsc --build","npm run lint","npm run format") and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","fetch(","eval(","atob(","base64")))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the child ProcessCommandLine and the referenced config file (`.vscode/tasks.json`, `.claude/setup.mjs`, etc.) on the host - benign ones are short and human-readable; Miasma/Hades versions contain heavily-obfuscated one-liners, fetch() to attacker infra, or eval of base64. SHA256 the config file against the StepSecurity advisory. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the child + IDE, snapshot the project directory for forensics, then rotate npm/PyPI/GitHub/cloud creds for the user. 3) Hunt: for every developer who opened the same repo (DeviceProcessEvents for `Code.exe` with the repo path in cmdline) in the last 14d - they're potentially infected even if they haven't run the tasks.json yet because folderOpen executes on first open.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode\\tasks.json",".vscode\\setup.mjs",".claude\\setup.mjs",".claude\\settings.json",".cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc",".gemini\\settings.json",".github\\setup.js")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)setup\.(mjs|mdc|js)"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode\\tasks.json",".vscode\\setup.mjs",".claude\\setup.mjs",".claude\\settings.json",".cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc",".gemini\\settings.json",".github\\setup.js")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)setup\.(mjs|mdc|js)"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IDE Auto-Loads Miasma/Hades Persistence Config on Project Open

      - '\claude-code.exe'

      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'

  cmdline_marker:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Code - Insiders.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\claude.exe OR *\\claude-code.exe OR *\\gemini.exe) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\bash.exe) (@CommandLine:*\\.vscode\\tasks.json* OR @CommandLine:*\\.vscode\\setup.mjs* OR @CommandLine:*\\.claude\\setup.mjs* OR @CommandLine:*\\.claude\\settings.json* OR @CommandLine:*\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc* OR @CommandLine:*\\.gemini\\settings.json* OR @CommandLine:*\\.github\\setup.js* OR @CommandLine:*setup.mjs* OR @CommandLine:*setup.mdc*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(Code|Code - Insiders|Cursor|claude|claude-code|gemini)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|bun|bash|python)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(\\.vscode\\\\(tasks\\.json|setup\\.mjs)|\\.claude\\\\(setup\\.mjs|settings\\.json)|\\.cursor\\\\rules\\\\setup\\.mdc|\\.gemini\\\\settings\\.json|\\.github\\\\setup\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\tasks.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc*" OR Processes.process="*\\.gemini\\settings.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.github\\setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mdc*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","python.exe","sh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\tasks.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc*" OR Processes.process="*\\.gemini\\settings.json*" OR Processes.process="*\\.github\\setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mdc*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Worm self-propagation: burst of npm publish / git push from a single developer host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the propagation step the article quantifies as '73 repositories in under two minutes' on the Microsoft Azure orgs - a single dev host using a stolen npm/GitHub token to republish or push to many destinations in a tight window. Thresholds 5+ publishes or 10+ pushes in 10 minutes from one identity, excluding known CI hosts. Rationale: Article: 'spread across 73 repositories in under two minutes' on Microsoft Azure orgs and 'republishes infected versions of every package that token can publish'. A real developer rarely publishes 5+ npm packages or pushes to 10+ git remotes in 10 minutes; the worm fan-out is the differentiator. Threshold tuned to be sensitive enough to catch the Microsoft Azure-scale burst (~73 in 2min ≈ 36 actions/min) while staying above a maintainer's normal commit-and-push cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://perplexityaimagazine.com/ai-news/miasma-worm-microsoft-github-supply-chain-attack-2026/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/binding-gyp-supply-chain-attack-compromises-dozens-of-npm-packages/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078.004 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Release engineer running `lerna publish` or `nx release publish` for a monorepo bulk release
  • Maintainer publishing a versioned set of related packages back-to-back
  • Developer rebasing a stack of branches and running `git push` for each
  • Git-flow style release where a feature-branch is pushed alongside main and a release tag
  • Bulk-rename or repo-migration tool legitimately pushing to many remotes
Suppression filter
| where not (SampleCmds has_any ("lerna publish","nx release","changeset publish","semantic-release"))  // legit monorepo bulk release tools
| where not (AccountName in~ ("release-eng","npm-publisher","github-actions[bot]"))  // known release identities
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full list of ProcessCommandLine in the 10-minute window - if they target distinct unrelated package names or unrelated org repos rather than a single monorepo, that's worm fan-out. Cross-reference the package names against the StepSecurity Miasma list (@vapi-ai/server-sdk, ai-sdk-ollama, jagreehal/*) and Hades list (ensmallen, embiggen, pyphetools, gpsea, ppkt2synergy). 2) Contain: revoke the npm token (`npm token revoke`), GitHub PAT, and any OIDC sessions for that user immediately. Force-yank affected versions via npm/PyPI security team contacts. Isolate the host. 3) Hunt: for each package the user just published, identify downstream npm consumers via DeviceFileEvents (npm install touching that package) over the last 24h - they're the next infection wave. Also pivot on UC1 to find the .vscode/.claude config files that landed before this burst.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") and ProcessCommandLine has "publish")
   or  (FileName =~ "git.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "push" and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--help")))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where DeviceName !startswith "ci-" and DeviceName !startswith "build-" and DeviceName !startswith "runner-" and DeviceName !startswith "gh-runner"
| summarize ActionCount = count(),
            DistinctCmds = dcount(ProcessCommandLine),
            SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            WindowSec = datetime_diff('second', max(Timestamp), min(Timestamp))
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") and ActionCount >= 5)
     or (FileName =~ "git.exe" and ActionCount >= 10)
| order by ActionCount desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") and ActingProcessCommandLine has "publish")
   or  (ActingProcessName has "git.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "push" and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--help")))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where DvcHostname !startswith "ci-" and DvcHostname !startswith "build-" and DvcHostname !startswith "runner-"
| summarize ActionCount = count(),
            DistinctCmds = dcount(ActingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where (ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") and ActionCount >= 5)
     or (ActingProcessName has "git.exe" and ActionCount >= 10)
| order by ActionCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd) AND @CommandLine:*publish*) OR (@Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*push* AND -@CommandLine:*--dry-run*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ((ImageFileName=/\\npm(\.exe|\.cmd)$/i AND CommandLine=/publish/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\git\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(?<!--dry-run.*)push/i))
| ComputerName!=/^(ci-|build-|runner-|gh-runner)/i
| bucket(span=10m, field=@timestamp, function=groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=count(as=ActionCount)))
| ActionCount >= 5
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.process_path) as paths min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") AND Processes.process="*publish*") OR (Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND Processes.process="*push*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 5 AND NOT match(user,"\$$") AND NOT match(host,"(?i)^(ci-|build-|runner-|agent-|gh-runner)")
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.process_path) as paths min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","npm.cmd") AND Processes.process="*publish*") OR (Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND Processes.process="*push*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 5 AND NOT match(user,"\$$") AND NOT match(host,"(?i)^(ci-|build-|runner-|agent-|gh-runner)")
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase

            - '\powershell.exe'

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Authorities dismantle 'AudiA6' ransomware crypto-laundering service

BleepingComputer
2026-06-11 7 use cases 2 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Law enforcement has dismantled the &ldquo;AudiA6&rdquo; cryptocurrency service&nbsp;allegedly used by ransomware actors and other cybercriminals to launder more than $380 million. [...]

ATT&CKT1190 T1486
Domainsaudia6.com dark2web.com
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Historical DNS/HTTP callouts to seized AudiA6 laundering and Dark2Web forum domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Historical DNS/HTTP callouts to seized AudiA6 laundering and Dark2Web forum domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts retrospectively (and going forward) for any DNS resolution or HTTP/TLS connection from internal hosts to audia6.com or dark2web.com, the cryptocurrency-laundering platform and underground forum seized by Europol and DOJ on 2026-06-10. A historical hit from a corporate endpoint suggests either (a) the host was used to route ransomware payouts via the AudiA6 mixer, or (b) a user/insider browsed the Dark2Web criminal marketplace — both warrant a full incident review of that host and account. Rationale: The article names two explicit domain IOCs (audia6.com, dark2web.com) that were seized in the 2026-06-10 Europol/DOJ takedown — Europol and the U.S. DOJ are cited in the article body as the primary sources confirming them, so the IOCs are second-source corroborated within the article itself. No further web search was needed: there are no actor, malware family, or TTP claims to validate beyond the seized infrastructure. The detection is a straightforward retrospective lookup over DNS, EDR network, and proxy telemetry — high-fidelity because the domains were dedicated cybercrime infrastructure with no legitimate use.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1657 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution Web Network_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC threat-intel analyst manually fetching one of the domains to validate the Europol IOC list from an EDR-monitored workstation
  • Sandbox / malware-analysis VM detonating a sample that beacons to one of the (now sinkholed) domains
  • Sinkhole or passive-DNS research host operated by the org's CTI team
  • Security-vendor crawler running from a corporate egress IP (rare but happens with on-prem sandboxes that VPN out via corp)
  • Browser tab left open from a journalist / researcher reading the BleepingComputer article — some readers paste the URL into the address bar
Suppression filter
// Defender: exclude documented CTI / sandbox hosts and analyst accounts
| where DeviceName !in~ ("cti-sandbox-01","cti-sandbox-02","soc-analyst-vdi-01")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountUpn !in~ ("cti-analyst1@corp.example","cti-analyst2@corp.example")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("cuckoo.exe","cape.exe","any.run.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull every hit for the affected host(s) and pivot on InitiatingProcess / browser process — is this a known SOC/CTI workstation legitimately validating IOCs, a sandbox, or an end-user endpoint? Check the user's role and whether they have a documented reason to touch cybercrime infrastructure. 2) Contain: if the host is an end-user endpoint with no analyst justification, isolate via Defender / Falcon network containment, force-reset the user's credentials (incl. AAD session revoke), and snapshot for forensics — historical AudiA6 traffic is consistent with ransomware payment routing or insider participation in cybercrime. 3) Hunt: enumerate all processes that resolved either domain in the last 180d, pivot on their parent processes and any binaries they wrote; cross-check the host's wallet files, browser history, and Telegram desktop artifacts for the blocked Dark2Web Telegram accounts; expand search to other Europol-published mule-account registration domains once that bundle i
let SeizedDomains = dynamic(["audia6.com","dark2web.com"]);
let LookbackDays = 180d;
let NetHits =
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (SeizedDomains)
           or RemoteUrl endswith ".audia6.com"
           or RemoteUrl endswith ".dark2web.com"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId,
              InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceNetworkEvents";
let DnsHits =
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess")
           or ActionType startswith "Dns"
    | where AdditionalFields has_any (SeizedDomains)
           or RemoteUrl has_any (SeizedDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId,
              InitiatingProcessAccountUpn = tostring(InitiatingProcessAccountName), InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceEvents/DNS";
union NetHits, DnsHits
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(),
            SampleProc = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl)
          by DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Source
| order by LastSeen desc
let SeizedDomains = dynamic(["audia6.com","dark2web.com"]);
let Lookback = 180d;
let DnsHits =
    DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where Name has_any (SeizedDomains)
           or Name endswith ".audia6.com" or Name endswith ".dark2web.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Source = "DnsEvents";
let ProxyHits =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where (isnotempty(DestinationHostName) and (DestinationHostName has_any (SeizedDomains) or DestinationHostName endswith ".audia6.com" or DestinationHostName endswith ".dark2web.com"))
         or (isnotempty(RequestURL) and (RequestURL has_any (SeizedDomains)))
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP,
              Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL),
              User = SourceUserName, Source = "Proxy/NGFW";
let AsimWeb =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where Url has_any (SeizedDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (SeizedDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr,
              Indicator = coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), User = SrcUsername, Source = "ImWebSession";
let AsimDns =
    ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (SeizedDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SrcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr,
              Indicator = DnsQuery, User = SrcUsername, Source = "ImDnsActivity";
union isfuzzy=true DnsHits, ProxyHits, AsimWeb, AsimDns
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            Indicators = make_set(Indicator, 10), Users = make_set(User, 10)
          by Computer, ClientIP, Source
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Connection to seized AudiA6 / Dark2Web cybercrime infrastructure
id: 7c8f4d2a-9e1b-4f6c-a3d8-2b5e9f1c8a4d
description: |
  Detects DNS resolutions to audia6.com or dark2web.com, the cryptocurrency
  laundering service and underground forum seized by Europol / DOJ on
  2026-06-10. Historical hits indicate the host either routed ransomware
  payouts through the AudiA6 mixer or accessed the Dark2Web forum.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/authorities-dismantle-audia6-ransomware-crypto-laundering-service/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1657
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - audia6.com
      - dark2web.com
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel research / IOC validation traffic from a known SOC analyst workstation
  - Sinkhole resolvers operated by the org's threat-intel team
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:(*audia6.com OR *AUDIA6.COM OR *dark2web.com OR *DARK2WEB.COM)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*audia6.com OR *AUDIA6.COM OR *dark2web.com OR *DARK2WEB.COM)) OR (source:zscaler @url:(*audia6.com* OR *dark2web.com*)) OR (source:linux.syslog @network.destination.domain:(*audia6.com OR *dark2web.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)(audia6|dark2web)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function={ count() | min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen) | max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen) })
| sort(LastSeen, order=desc)
| union([
    #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/.+/
    | join({ #event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)(audia6|dark2web)\.com$/i }, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[DomainName])
    | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName], function=count())
  ])
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query IN ("audia6.com","*.audia6.com","dark2web.com","*.dark2web.com") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer host
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| append [
  | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.url IN ("*audia6.com*","*dark2web.com*") OR Web.dest IN ("audia6.com","*.audia6.com","dark2web.com","*.dark2web.com") by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.dest Web.http_user_agent
  | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
  | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
  | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Medium

GitHub to Automate Disable npm Script Installs to Block Supply Chain Attacks

Cyber Security News
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced a major security-focused update to the Node Package Manager (npm), introducing breaking changes in the upcoming npm v12 release to reduce software supply chain attack risks significantly. The update, expected in July 2026, will turn off automatic execution of installation scripts by default, one of the most commonly abused mechanisms in malicious [&#8230;] The post GitHub to Automate Disable npm Script Installs to Block Supply Chain Attacks appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents

| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or SHA1 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or MD5 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or SHA1 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e") or MD5 in~ ("9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767", "7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae", "241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05", "522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — npm v12 delivers one of the biggest security improvements in years
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Node/npm parent spawning network or scripting child during package install · [LLM] Known malicious npm-supply-chain package SHA256 observed on disk or executed · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound to Shai-Hulud / npm-worm C2 (webhook.site, sfrclak.com, 142.11.206.73) from node/npm process tree · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog secret-scanner binary execution on developer or CI endpoint · [LLM] Node/npm/bun process touching SSH, npm or GitHub credential files · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Node/npm parent spawning network or scripting child during package install AIInstallation Medium
Detects node/npm/yarn/pnpm processes spawning curl, wget, bun, powershell, mshta, cmd or sh — the postinstall/preinstall script execution chain abused by Nx s1ngularity, Shai-Hulud, axios hijack, and Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm campaigns to drop second-stage payloads on developer and CI machines. Rationale: Pivots on the exact behavioural chain the article calls out — `When anyone runs npm install, npm runs that script automatically as the user` followed by `downloads the real payload from an attacker server`. Anchors on node/npm/yarn/pnpm as parents and adds article-IOC strings (webhook.site, sfrclak.com, 142.11.206.73, bun.sh, trufflehog) for high-fidelity matches.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Native-module packages (node-gyp, sharp, canvas, bcrypt, node-sass) invoking curl/wget to fetch prebuilt binaries from GitHub during install
  • Playwright/Cypress/Puppeteer postinstall hooks downloading browser binaries
  • Husky/lefthook installing git hooks via shell child processes
  • Corporate-internal scaffolding tools (yo, create-react-app, nx) that legitimately call PowerShell during init
  • CI runners executing npm ci followed by helper scripts that shell out for asset downloads
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","playwright install","cypress install","puppeteer","electron","husky install") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("webhook.site","sfrclak.com","142.11.206.73","trufflehog"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full parent ProcessCommandLine — confirm it was an `install`/`ci` invocation, identify the package name from the cwd path (e.g. `node_modules\<pkg>`), and look up the package + version against npm registry and Aikido/Socket malware feeds. Check if the child made network connections to webhook.site/sfrclak.com/142.11.206.73. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, rotate any GitHub PAT, npm token, SSH key, AWS key and cloud session token stored in the user profile, force-revoke npm tokens via `npm token revoke`, and remove the package from node_modules + lockfile. 3) Hunt: pivot on the package name across all hosts that ran `npm install` against the same lockfile in the last 14d; query DeviceNetworkEvents for the same SHA256 contacting any of the IOC IPs/domains; check for new public GitHub repos created by the user's PAT.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","postinstall","preinstall","run-script"," ci ","npm exec","npx ") 
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhook.site","sfrclak.com","142.11.206.73","trufflehog","bun install","bun.sh","Invoke-WebRequest","Invoke-RestMethod","curl -fsSL","wget -q")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

description: Detects node, npm, yarn or pnpm spawning curl, wget, powershell, bun or other shell/scripting binaries during a package install — the postinstall lifecycle script execution chain used by Nx s1ngularity, Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud npm worms.

Outbound to Shai-Hulud / npm-worm C2 (webhook.site, sfrclak.com, 142.11.206.73) from node/npm process tree AICommand & Control High
High-fidelity network detection for the article-specific C2 indicators — webhook.site, sfrclak.com and 142.11.206.73 — when the originating process is node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun or a child spawned underneath them. Catches the first-stage beacon and credential exfiltration steps common to Nx s1ngularity, Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud campaigns. Rationale: Anchors on three explicit article IOCs (142.11.206.73, sfrclak.com, webhook.site) and pins them to a node/npm process tree to eliminate the noise of webhook.site being used for general webhook testing. Article quote: `It fingerprints the machine, downloads the real payload from an attacker server, runs it`.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1567.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately testing a webhook.site URL via Node fetch/axios during integration work — distinguishable by ad-hoc REPL context vs install-time
  • QA/staging environments using webhook.site as a test sink for outbound webhooks
  • Internal SRE tooling that pipes test traffic through webhook.site to validate egress
  • Curl/wget invoked manually under a CI npm job for an unrelated artifact pull from one of these hosts (low likelihood)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "webhook-test" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\test\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent — confirm whether this fired inside an npm install lifecycle (parent cmdline contains `install`, `postinstall`, cwd is under `node_modules`). Capture the webhook.site path (often a unique UUID) and the package name. 2) Contain: block the destination at egress proxy/firewall, isolate the host, revoke any npm/GitHub/AWS/SSH credentials stored on the device or accessible to the user, and pull the malicious package version from any internal mirror. 3) Hunt: search the last 30d of DeviceNetworkEvents for the same RemoteIP/RemoteUrl across the estate, query EmailEvents for phishing targeting maintainers of any in-house packages, and check GitHub audit logs for new public repos or pushed branches with names like `shai-hulud` or `Shai-Hulud-Migration`.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "142.11.206.73"
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("webhook.site","sfrclak.com")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","node","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, 
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "142.11.206.73"
   or DstHostname has_any ("webhook.site","sfrclak.com")
   or Url has_any ("webhook.site","sfrclak.com","142.11.206.73")
| extend SrcProcess = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventOriginalUid)).process)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TruffleHog secret-scanner binary execution on developer or CI endpoint AIActions on Objectives High
Detects execution of the TruffleHog secret-scanner binary on developer/CI hosts — Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud worms drop TruffleHog as the credential-harvest stage to scrape GitHub tokens, npm credentials, AWS keys and SSH keys before exfiltration. TruffleHog has almost no legitimate runtime use on developer endpoints outside dedicated security tooling. Rationale: Article explicitly names TruffleHog as the secret-scrape tool in Shai-Hulud: `ran TruffleHog to scrape secrets, and dumped them into public GitHub repos`. The binary name + canonical subcommand patterns (`trufflehog filesystem`, `trufflehog github`) are unique to this tool — extremely low false-positive surface outside known security-team usage.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised security/DevSecOps team running scheduled secret scans against internal repos — should be allowlisted by service-account name + host
  • Pre-commit hooks running trufflehog locally for developers who installed it themselves
  • GitHub Actions self-hosted runners executing trufflehog-actions on PR scanning
  • Internal CI pipelines piping trufflehog output to artifact storage
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("svc-secscan","svc-devsecops") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\security-tools\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent process and command line — confirm whether trufflehog was spawned by an npm install context (`node.exe` / `npm.cmd` ancestor) vs a known security-team service account. Identify the scan target from the cmdline. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke every credential reachable from the user's profile (GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access keys, SSH keys, browser-stored secrets), and force-rotate them. Pull the originating npm package + version. 3) Hunt: search DeviceNetworkEvents for follow-on POSTs from this host to webhook.site, sfrclak.com or 142.11.206.73; query GitHub audit logs for new public repos created by the impacted PAT within the next 24h (Shai-Hulud's exfil destination); look for the same trufflehog SHA256 across the estate.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","trufflehog3.exe","trufflehog3","th.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog github","trufflehog git --","trufflehog gitlab","trufflehog s3","trufflehog --only-verified")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcImage = FolderPath,
          ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("trufflehog.exe","trufflehog","trufflehog3.exe","trufflehog3")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog github","trufflehog git --","trufflehog gitlab","trufflehog s3","trufflehog --only-verified")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Node/npm/bun process touching SSH, npm or GitHub credential files AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects node/npm/bun and their child processes reading or writing under credential-bearing paths (~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/gh, ~/.aws, ~/.docker, crypto wallet directories) — the discovery + credential-access behaviour every observed npm install-time worm performs after the initial postinstall script fires. Rationale: Targets the discovery/credential-access pattern called out by the kill-chain block: `the payload scans for tokens, SSH keys, and other goodies`. Pivots on the article-specific actor lineage — node/npm/bun reaching into ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/gh, wallet stores — which is anomalous outside the install of one or two specific tools.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083 T1217
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm itself reading ~/.npmrc for registry auth during routine install — high-volume; needs allowlist of .npmrc-only access from npm.cmd parent
  • Yarn 2+ reading ~/.npmrc and ~/.yarnrc.yml for shared registry token
  • gh CLI extensions written in Node calling into ~/.config/gh
  • AWS SDK in Node app reading ~/.aws/credentials at process startup (long-running services, not install-time)
  • Crypto wallet dev tooling (Hardhat, Truffle) legitimately reading Ethereum keystore directories during local testing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "npm.cmd" and FileName =~ ".npmrc" and ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified") and tostring(FolderPath) endswith @"\")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yarn install","yarn add","yarn config") and FileName == ".npmrc")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the parent chain — is this `npm.cmd → node.exe` during install (suspicious) or `node.exe` as a long-running app process (likely benign). Pull the cwd to identify the calling package and check whether the user-account session shows a fresh `npm install`/`npm ci`/`yarn install` in the last 30 minutes. 2) Contain: if install-context confirmed, isolate the host, force-rotate every credential type read (SSH, npm, GitHub PAT, AWS, crypto-wallet seeds), and remove the package + version from node_modules and lockfile. 3) Hunt: pivot on the SHA256 of the InitiatingProcessParentFile across the estate; query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to webhook.site/sfrclak.com/142.11.206.73 from the same host within ±10 min; check GitHub audit log for the user's PAT being used from new IPs in the next 24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","node","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.ssh\", @"\.aws\", @"\.npmrc", @"\.config\gh\", @"\.docker\config.json", @"\AppData\Roaming\npm\", @"\AppData\Roaming\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\AppData\Roaming\Solana\", @"\AppData\Local\Yarn\")
   or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa",".npmrc","credentials","config.json","hosts.json","wallet.dat")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "node_modules\\.bin\\eslint"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc

title: Node or npm Process Accessing SSH npm or GitHub Credential Files
id: e1d2c3b4-5a6b-4709-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d
description: Detects node, npm, yarn, pnpm or bun (or a child process spawned underneath them) opening files inside .ssh, .aws, .npmrc, .config/gh, .docker, npm token cache or crypto-wallet keystore directories — the credential-discovery stage Nx s1ngularity, Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud worms perform after their postinstall script fires.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
author: SOC Detection Eng
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1217
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.cmd'
      - '\yarn.cmd'
      - '\pnpm.cmd'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
  selection_paths:
    - TargetFilename|contains:
        - '\.ssh\'
        - '\.aws\credentials'
        - '\.npmrc'
        - '\.config\gh\'
        - '\.docker\config.json'
        - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
        - '\Solana\'
    - TargetFilename|endswith:
        - '\id_rsa'
        - '\id_ed25519'
        - '\wallet.dat'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_paths
falsepositives:
  - npm itself legitimately reading ~/.npmrc for registry config during install — pair with absence-of-known-pkg context
  - Yarn reading ~/.npmrc for shared auth config
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.cmd OR *\npx.cmd OR *\yarn.cmd OR *\pnpm.cmd OR *\bun.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\python.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\.ssh\* OR *\.SSH\* OR *\.aws\credentials* OR *\.npmrc* OR *\.NPMRC* OR *\.config\gh\* OR *\.docker\config.json* OR *\Ethereum\keystore\* OR *\Solana\* OR *\id_rsa OR *\id_ed25519 OR *\wallet.dat)
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|bun|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh|python|python3|bash|sh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\\\\\.ssh\\\\|\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|\\\\\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.config\\\\gh\\\\|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|Ethereum\\\\keystore|Solana|\\\\id_rsa$|\\\\id_ed25519$|wallet\\.dat$)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Known malicious npm-supply-chain package SHA256 observed on disk or executed AIInstallation Medium
IOC-driven detection for the eight SHA256 file hashes tied to the Nx s1ngularity / Shai-Hulud / axios hijack / Mini Shai-Hulud malicious package corpus. Hits indicate the host pulled a compromised version into node_modules or executed the dropped payload. Rationale: Direct SHA256 / SHA1 hash IOCs supplied alongside the article — the highest-fidelity signal available. Each hit indicates the host pulled or executed a known-malicious package version from Nx s1ngularity / Shai-Hulud / axios / Mini Shai-Hulud. No behavioural inference required.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal malware sandbox or detonation host intentionally fetching the package for analysis — should be allowlisted by hostname/group
  • DFIR analyst manually downloading the indicator file to a forensic workstation for triage
  • Vulnerability-scanning tooling caching indicator files for signature testing
  • Threat-intel platform agent (Tines/Anomali/Recorded Future) syncing IOC bundles to disk — pair filter excludes their service-account paths
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the FolderPath of the hit — confirm it is under `node_modules\<pkg>`, identify the exact package + version, and look up the package against npm registry. Cross-reference the host's `package-lock.json` and CI history. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke and rotate every credential reachable from the user's profile (npm token via `npm token revoke`, GitHub PAT, AWS access keys, SSH keys, browser-stored secrets, crypto wallet seeds), and purge the package from the project + lockfile. Search for and revoke any new public GitHub repos created by the affected PAT. 3) Hunt: query last 60d of DeviceFileEvents for the same SHA256 across every host; pivot DeviceNetworkEvents to look for the same host beaconing webhook.site/sfrclak.com/142.11.206.73; query GitHub audit logs for the impacted user account showing publish-token use against unrelated packages (lateral worm spread).

Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:

detection:

level: high
ENDPOINT

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
