SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callout (any process) AICommand & Control High
Broad-spectrum hunt for any process on any host contacting the SPECTRALVIPER C2 domain or IP list named by ESET, including the second campaign's gatewayrvcenter[.]com (Vietnamese transport construction corp). Catches SPECTRALVIPER variants where the injection target differs from OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, and the loader stages that beacon before injection completes. Rationale: Six C2 domains and eight IPs explicitly tied to OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER infrastructure across both campaigns. financemachinelearning[.]com and gatewayrvcenter[.]com are named directly in the ESET article body; the remaining four domains and the IPs come from the pre-extracted IOC bundle and align with the broader campaign infrastructure. Two distinct kill-chain campaigns share this list, so any hit warrants alerting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VirusTotal / urlscan / Hybrid Analysis reputation lookups from analyst workstations (filter on SOC subnet)
  • Threat-intel feed processors hitting the domains to enrich indicators (filter on TIP service accounts)
  • Sandbox detonations in security research VMs
  • Sinkholed IPs after takedown returning legitimate-looking traffic for retrospective post-mortem
  • Vendor EDR threat-feed validation calls
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","vt-cli.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Determine if the connecting host runs FireAnt Metakit (FireAnt campaign scope) or has a public-facing MSSQL server (transport construction corp scope). Pull the InitiatingProcess and check whether it's OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (UC #3 territory), Metakit.exe / setup.exe (UC #1), or sqlservr.exe (initial-access pivot). 2) CONTAIN: Block all six domains and all eight IPs at the proxy/firewall immediately — they cover both campaigns. Isolate the host. Hash any binaries in InitiatingProcessFolderPath and compare against the UC #5 SHA1 list. 3) HUNT: Pivot from each matched IP using passive DNS — adversary may use additional FQDNs not in this list. Search the previous 180 days for the same RemoteIP across all hosts. Run UC #2 (DtlCrashCatch.dll) and UC #5 (SHA1 match) estate-wide.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains) or RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            HitCount = count(),
            Procs = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 32),
            Cmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 32),
            Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 16),
            Destinations = make_set(coalesce(RemoteUrl, tostring(RemoteIP)), 16)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen asc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains) or DestinationIP in (C2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, DeviceVendor),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where Name has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER / FireAnt downloader SHA1 IOC hash hunt AIInstallation Medium
Retroactive hunt for the five SHA1 hashes published with the OceanLotus FireAnt / transport construction campaigns. Covers execution, file write, and image load — catches the downloader, the side-loaded DLL, and the SPECTRALVIPER payload variants ESET captured during the 2024-2026 intrusions. Rationale: Five SHA1 hashes from the pre-extracted IOC bundle covering the OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER tooling. Targeting process create + file write + image load gives the widest possible retroactive coverage — catches the downloader (UC #1), the side-loaded DLL (UC #2), and the SPECTRALVIPER payload binaries. ESET's welivesecurity report is the authoritative source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1027 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike / VT scanning the IOC samples after analyst submission — InitiatingProcessFileName will be MsMpEng / SenseIR / etc.
  • Malware-analysis sandbox VMs detonating the samples (filter on the sandbox host subnet)
  • Threat-intel platform retroactively pulling samples from a malware feed
  • Endpoint full-disk hash inventory job hitting a quarantined sample
Suppression filter
| where ParentImage !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe","vt-cli.exe","7zG.exe","7z.exe") and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine\"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: For each hit, identify the file path and parent process. Pull EventClass: ProcessCreate hits are 'live execution' (highest severity); FileWrite is 'on disk' (still concerning if recent); ImageLoad means a process actively side-loaded the artefact. Check whether the host runs FireAnt Metakit or has public-facing MSSQL. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate every host with a match. Quarantine the file using Defender Live Response. Add the SHA1s to your tenant indicator block-list to prevent re-execution. Capture memory of any process whose image was the matched hash. 3) HUNT: For each hit, pivot on the surrounding 1-hour window — pull DeviceNetworkEvents (UC #4 C2 list), DeviceProcessEvents for child processes spawned by the matched binary, and DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll. Sweep the estate for the same file name and same parent process chain on other hosts.
let KnownSha1 = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"
]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "ProcessCreate", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventClass = "ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let KnownSha1 = dynamic([
  "865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D",
  "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194",
  "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947",
  "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB",
  "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where SHA1 in (KnownSha1) or Hash in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EvtType = "ProcessCreate", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA1),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in (KnownSha1) or Hash in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EvtType = "FileWrite", TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName),
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where FileHash has_any (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, EvtType = "4688", NewProcessName, CommandLine, FileHash),
  (ThreatIntelligenceIndicator
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
    | where FileHashValue in (KnownSha1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = "(TI match)", EvtType = "ThreatIntel", IndicatorId, FileHashValue, ThreatType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP POST to Oracle PeopleSoft deserialization endpoints (gadget chain initial access) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PeopleSoft Tuxedo / Java app-server spawning shells (post-exploit RCE)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection or DNS to ShinyHunters PeopleSoft campaign infrastructure · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Large outbound HTTPS upload from PeopleSoft application or database server · [LLM] Bulk SELECT or export from PeopleSoft student / finance tables
HTTP POST to Oracle PeopleSoft deserialization endpoints (gadget chain initial access) AIExploitation Medium
Detects POST requests targeting Oracle PeopleSoft (PSFT) Tuxedo/PIA endpoints that are commonly abused by ShinyHunters' 'gadget chain' of zero-day + known deserialization bugs. Focuses on PeopleSoft-specific URI stems and oversized request bodies indicative of serialized Java payloads. Rationale: Targets the PeopleSoft 'gadget chain' explicitly named in the article. PSFT-specific URI stems (/psp/, /psc/, /PSIGW/, IntegrationGateway) + oversized POST bodies are the signature of Java/Tuxedo deserialization exploits. Cross-checked Oracle CPU advisories and prior CVE-2023-22054 / CVE-2023-22102 PeopleSoft deserialization research. Cross-checked against: • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PeopleSoft integration broker traffic from partner systems (HR, payroll, SIS connectors)
  • PeopleTools upgrade installers POSTing large payloads to /psc/
  • Internal load testing against PIA endpoints
  • Mobile PeopleSoft Fluid UI POSTs containing large form payloads
  • Legitimate large file uploads via PeopleSoft attachment service
Suppression filter
and cIP !in ("<partner_integration_ip_1>","<partner_integration_ip_2>")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull full request body via WAF/reverse proxy for the matched POST; look for Java serialization magic bytes (AC ED 00 05), gadget-class names (CommonsBeanutils, Tuxedo PSFT_*), or readObject markers. Confirm caller IP is not in the partner integration allowlist. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the edge WAF; if exploitation indicators present, isolate the PSFT app-server VM and snapshot for forensics; rotate any service-account credentials with PSFT DB access. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot from the PSFT host on DeviceProcessEvents for child processes of PSAPPSRV/PSPRCSRV/java.exe; query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to 142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24, or azurenetfiles.net; check DB audit logs for bulk SELECT on PS_STUDENT_/PS_FINANCE_ tables.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAPPSRV.exe","PSPRCSRV.exe","tuxedo.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80,443,8000,8080,8443,7777)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("/psp/","/psc/","/PSIGW/","/peoplesoft/","/cs/ps/","PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector","IntegrationGateway")
| where csBytes > 50000 or csUriStem has_any ("PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector","IntegrationGateway")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, csBytes, sPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious POST to Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget-Chain Endpoints
id: 5a8e1d2c-4f7b-4c9a-9e2f-1b3d4a6c7e8d
description: Detects POST requests to known PeopleSoft PIA/Tuxedo/IntegrationGateway endpoints associated with the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft gadget-chain campaign that breached University of Nottingham and 100+ orgs.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/psp/'
      - '/psc/'
      - '/PSIGW/'
      - '/peoplesoft/'
      - '/cs/ps/'
      - 'PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector'
      - 'IntegrationGateway'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:(windows.security OR linux.syslog) (@http.method:POST OR @CommandLine:POST) (@http.url:(*\/psp\/* OR *\/psc\/* OR *\/PSIGW\/* OR *\/peoplesoft\/* OR *PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector* OR *IntegrationGateway*))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(PSAPPSRV|PSPRCSRV|tuxedo|java|javaw|w3wp|httpd|nginx)\.exe$/i
| RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=8000 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=8443 OR RemotePort=7777
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.bytes_in) as bytes_in from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST (Web.url="*/psp/*" OR Web.url="*/psc/*" OR Web.url="*/PSIGW/*" OR Web.url="*/peoplesoft/*" OR Web.url="*/cs/ps/*") (Web.bytes_in>50000 OR Web.url="*PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector*" OR Web.url="*IntegrationGateway*") by Web.dest Web.http_user_agent Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where status<500
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.src) as src values(Web.bytes_in) as bytes_in from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST (Web.url="*/psp/*" OR Web.url="*/psc/*" OR Web.url="*/PSIGW/*" OR Web.url="*/peoplesoft/*" OR Web.url="*/cs/ps/*") (Web.bytes_in>50000 OR Web.url="*PeopleSoftServiceListeningConnector*" OR Web.url="*IntegrationGateway*") by Web.dest Web.http_user_agent Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where status<500
PeopleSoft Tuxedo / Java app-server spawning shells (post-exploit RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects the textbook deserialization RCE outcome: PeopleSoft PSAPPSRV/PSPRCSRV/Tuxedo/java processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, or staging tools. This is the execution stage of the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft gadget-chain campaign. Rationale: Article states 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' resulting in RCE on PeopleSoft. PeopleSoft application server processes (PSAPPSRV, PSPRCSRV, Tuxedo BBL) spawning a shell or LOLBin is a near-zero-FP indicator of successful deserialization exploitation. This is the canonical execution-phase pivot for PeopleSoft compromise. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/ • https://docs.oracle.com/cd/F69094_01/pt860pbr5/eng/pt/tsvr/concept_PeopleSoftServerProcesses.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PeopleSoft Application Engine programs legitimately calling cmd.exe wrappers for OS file operations
  • SQR/COBOL batch jobs invoking shells for archive cleanup
  • PeopleSoft DBA scripts run via PSADMIN for legitimate maintenance
  • Oracle PeopleTools patch installers spawning command shells
  • Custom shell-out logic in legacy Application Engine PeopleCode
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PSADMIN","AE_DAEMON","PTUPGRADE") and AccountName endswith "_psadmin")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full command line of the child process; check for download/exec patterns (Invoke-WebRequest, IEX, certutil -urlcache, base64). Correlate with W3CIISLog for an incoming POST to /psp/, /psc/, /PSIGW/, or IntegrationGateway in the preceding 60s. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the PeopleSoft host with EDR network containment; suspend PSAPPSRV service to stop further child-process spawning; snapshot for forensics. Rotate the PSFT service-account password and DB credentials. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all PSFT app-server fleet for the same parent->child pattern in the last 30 days; query DeviceFileEvents for archives (.zip/.7z/.tar) written by PSAPPSRV/java in the past week; check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to the campaign IPs/domain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAPPSRV.exe","PSPRCSRV.exe","PSADMIN.exe","tuxedo.exe","tmboot.exe","BBL.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","sh","bash","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("PSAPPSRV.exe","PSPRCSRV.exe","PSADMIN.exe","tuxedo.exe","tmboot.exe","BBL.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Oracle PeopleSoft App-Server Spawning Shell or LOLBin
id: a2c8f6e1-9b3d-4f2a-8c5e-7d4b1a9c0e2f
description: Detects PeopleSoft / Tuxedo / Java application server processes spawning interactive shells or download LOLBins. Indicator of post-exploit RCE from the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft gadget-chain campaign that hit University of Nottingham and 100+ organizations.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:

  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\PSAPPSRV.exe'
      - '\PSPRCSRV.exe'
      - '\PSADMIN.exe'
      - '\tuxedo.exe'
      - '\tmboot.exe'
      - '\BBL.exe'
      - '\java.exe'
      - '\javaw.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'

      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child

Outbound connection or DNS to ShinyHunters PeopleSoft campaign infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any host (especially application/database server VLANs) contacting the ShinyHunters campaign IP block 142.11.200.186-190, the supporting addresses 108.174.202.99 / 176.120.22.24, or DNS lookups for azurenetfiles.net used by the actor for staging/exfiltration of stolen PeopleSoft data. Rationale: Article ships explicit IOC IPs (142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) and the lookalike domain azurenetfiles.net used by ShinyHunters in the PeopleSoft campaign. Any contact from an internal host — particularly server VLANs hosting PeopleSoft — is high-confidence indicator of compromise. Cross-checked phase 5/6 IOC block from kill-chain reconstruction. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scanning hosts deliberately probing campaign IPs for telemetry
  • Researcher VMs running sandbox detonations against the IOCs
  • Honeypot infrastructure attracting attacker callbacks
  • Lookalike-domain typosquat reports - 'azurenetfiles.net' may resemble legit azurewebsites.net so misconfigured DNS forwarders could query
  • Legitimate Azure file storage requests mistyped to azurenetfiles.net
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and DeviceName !startswith "sandbox-" and DeviceName !startswith "honeypot-"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the contacting host, its VLAN/role (is it a PeopleSoft app or DB server?), and the initiating process. Pull a 24h timeline of egress bytes from the host to detect bulk exfil. Step 2 (contain): EDR network-isolate the host; block the IP block 142.11.200.0/24 + 108.174.202.99 + 176.120.22.24 at perimeter firewall; sinkhole azurenetfiles.net at internal DNS. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep CommonSecurityLog/DeviceNetworkEvents fleet-wide for the same IOCs over 90d; pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for PSAPPSRV/java spawning archive utilities (7z, zip, tar) preceding the egress; check DB audit logs for bulk PII queries on the same host.

let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["azurenetfiles.net"]);
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| union (DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

| where AdditionalFields has "azurenetfiles.net"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc

title: ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Campaign C2 / Exfil Infrastructure Contact
id: 7e1f4b8d-3a6c-4d9e-b8f2-2c5a7e1b3d9f

Large outbound HTTPS upload from PeopleSoft application or database server AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for sustained multi-gigabyte outbound transfers from servers hosting Oracle PeopleSoft (PSFT) to non-corporate destinations — matches the 40GB+ exfiltration profile claimed by ShinyHunters against Nottingham and 100+ orgs. Rationale: Article quantifies the exfil: '40GB of documents containing student finance data, billing and payment information, credit card and payment details, and campus portal exports'. Combining a PeopleSoft/Oracle/archive-utility source process with sustained multi-GB outbound HTTPS to public destinations matches the campaign's exfil profile across all 100+ victims. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1567 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PeopleSoft data warehouse exports to a cloud SFTP partner
  • Database backup uploads to S3/Azure Blob from Oracle hosts
  • Veeam/CommVault cloud-tier backup egress
  • Legitimate ETL jobs pushing transformed PeopleSoft data to a BI cloud (Snowflake, BigQuery)
  • WSUS/SCCM cache sync from server VLAN
Suppression filter
| where DestinationHostName !endswith ".amazonaws.com" and DestinationHostName !endswith ".blob.core.windows.net" and DestinationHostName !endswith ".veeam.com" and DestinationHostName !endswith ".commvault.com"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the source host's role (PSFT app, PSFT DB, ETL gateway?) and the destination autonomous system / ASN owner. Compare the egress volume against the host's 30-day P95 baseline. Step 2 (contain): If the destination is not on the corporate allow-list (cloud backup endpoints, known SFTP partners), EDR-isolate the host; block destination at perimeter; preserve memory + disk for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for recent archive-creation activity (7z/rar/tar) on the same host; query DB audit logs for bulk SELECT on PS_STUDENT_/PS_FINANCE_ tables in the preceding 24h; check for child processes of PSAPPSRV/java spawning curl/powershell with Invoke-WebRequest.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAPPSRV.exe","PSPRCSRV.exe","tuxedo.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","oracle.exe","tnslsnr.exe","7z.exe","7za.exe","WinRAR.exe","rar.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| summarize ConnectionCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Destinations = make_set(RemoteIP, 50), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 50) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where ConnectionCount > 100
| order by ConnectionCount desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Palo Alto Networks","Fortinet","Cisco","Check Point","Zscaler")
| where CommunicationDirection in ("outbound","1","Outbound") or isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where SourceHostName has_any ("psft","peoplesoft","-ps-","-orcl","-tux") or SourceIP startswith "10." 
| summarize TotalBytesOut = sum(toint(SentBytes)), Connections = count() by SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where TotalBytesOut > 1073741824
| extend GB_Out = round(todouble(TotalBytesOut)/1073741824, 2)
| order by TotalBytesOut desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:3 @Image:(*\PSAPPSRV.exe OR *\psappsrv.exe OR *\PSPRCSRV.exe OR *\java.exe OR *\Java.exe OR *\tuxedo.exe OR *\7z.exe OR *\WinRAR.exe OR *\rar.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe) @DestinationPort:(443 OR 80 OR 8443) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| ContextImageFileName=/(PSAPPSRV|PSPRCSRV|tuxedo|java|javaw|oracle|tnslsnr|7z|7za|WinRAR|rar|curl|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=8443
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
| count > 100
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, bytes, action
| filter action = "ACCEPT" and dstPort in [443, 80, 8443]
| filter not (dstAddr like /^10\./ or dstAddr like /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\./ or dstAddr like /^192\.168\./)
| stats sum(bytes) as total_bytes_out by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, bin(1h) as hour
| filter total_bytes_out > 1073741824
| sort total_bytes_out desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as total_bytes_out count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app=ssl OR All_Traffic.dest_port IN (443,80,8443) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search src="*psft*" OR src="*peoplesoft*" OR src="*-ps-*" OR src="*-orcl*" OR src="*-tux*" | where total_bytes_out > 1073741824 | eval gb_out=round(total_bytes_out/1073741824,2) | table src dest_ip dest gb_out count
| tstats summariesonly=false sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as total_bytes_out count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app=ssl OR All_Traffic.dest_port IN (443,80,8443) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search src="*psft*" OR src="*peoplesoft*" OR src="*-ps-*" OR src="*-orcl*" OR src="*-tux*" | where total_bytes_out > 1073741824 | eval gb_out=round(total_bytes_out/1073741824,2) | table src dest_ip dest gb_out count
Bulk SELECT or export from PeopleSoft student / finance tables AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for bulk read access against PeopleSoft student-record and finance tables (PS_STUDENT_*, PS_STDNT_*, PS_FIN_*, PS_CC_*) — the exact data classes ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen from Nottingham (names, addresses, passport numbers, fee/payment data, credit-card details). Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates the stolen data classes: 'student finance data, billing and payment information, credit card and payment details, and campus portal exports' plus 'names, addresses, phone numbers, ethnicities, disabilities, passport numbers'. PeopleSoft canonical table prefixes for this data are PS_STUDENT_*, PS_STDNT_*, PS_FIN_*, PS_CC_* (credit card), PS_PAYMENT_*, PS_BILLING_*. Bulk SELECT against these by an unusual user/host is high signal. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E83876_01/psft/index.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1213 T1005 T1560
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate financial-aid reporting jobs by University finance staff
  • Term-end batch billing runs touching PS_BILLING / PS_FIN tables
  • Regulatory reporting exports (HESA, IRS-1098T, ICEF) hitting student tables
  • DBA-led PS_STUDENT_* table cardinality analysis during a PeopleTools upgrade
  • BI / data-warehouse ETL pulling nightly snapshots of student records
Suppression filter
| where DB_USER !in ("REPORTING_SVC","ETL_SVC","HESA_REPORT") and CLIENT_PROGRAM_NAME !in ("informatica","ssis","talend")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the executing DB user, OS user, and client program; compare against the list of approved ETL/finance batch jobs and reporting service accounts. Confirm the host generating the SELECTs is a sanctioned BI/ETL host, not a PSFT app server unexpectedly running ad-hoc queries. Step 2 (contain): If the source is the PSFT app server itself (PSAPPSRV/java initiating the SELECTs out-of-band), revoke the session, kill the DB session, isolate the host, rotate the PSFT service-account password and Oracle DB credentials. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to DeviceFileEvents for archive/CSV creation by the same process; check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from the host to the campaign IPs (142.11.200.0/24, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) or azurenetfiles.net; sweep PSFT fleet for the same query pattern in the prior 30 days.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PSAPPSRV.exe","PSPRCSRV.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","oracle.exe","sqlplus.exe","expdp.exe","exp.exe","sqlcmd.exe")
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".csv" or FileName endswith ".dmp" or FileName endswith ".sql" or FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".7z" or FileName endswith ".rar" or FileName endswith ".tar" or FileName endswith ".gz" or FileName endswith ".xlsx"
| where FileSize > 50000000
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize
| order by FileSize desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Facility in ("local0","local1","daemon") or ProcessName has "oracle"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("PS_STUDENT","PS_STDNT","PS_FIN_","PS_CC_","PS_PAYMENT","PS_BILLING")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("SELECT","EXPORT","EXPDP")
| extend TablesTouched = extract_all(@"PS_[A-Z_]+", SyslogMessage)
| summarize EventCount = count(), DistinctTables = dcount_array(TablesTouched), Tables = make_set(TablesTouched, 50) by Computer, HostIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where EventCount > 50 or DistinctTables > 5
| order by EventCount desc
source:(linux.syslog OR linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (PS_STUDENT* OR PS_STDNT* OR PS_FIN_* OR PS_CC_* OR PS_PAYMENT* OR PS_BILLING*) (SELECT OR EXPORT OR expdp OR exp)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/(PSAPPSRV|PSPRCSRV|java|javaw|oracle|sqlplus|expdp|exp|sqlcmd)\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(csv|dmp|sql|zip|7z|rar|tar|gz|xlsx)$/i
| WrittenBytes>50000000
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
CLOUD
index=oracle_audit OR sourcetype="oracle:audit" OR sourcetype="db:audit" (action_name=SELECT OR statement=SELECT*) (OBJECT_NAME="PS_STUDENT*" OR OBJECT_NAME="PS_STDNT*" OR OBJECT_NAME="PS_FIN_*" OR OBJECT_NAME="PS_CC_*" OR OBJECT_NAME="PS_PAYMENT*" OR OBJECT_NAME="PS_BILLING*" OR SQL_TEXT="*PS_STUDENT*" OR SQL_TEXT="*PS_STDNT*" OR SQL_TEXT="*PS_FIN_*" OR SQL_TEXT="*PS_CC_*") | stats count dc(OBJECT_NAME) as tables_touched values(OBJECT_NAME) as tables sum(rows_processed) as total_rows by DB_USER OS_USER USERHOST CLIENT_PROGRAM_NAME | where tables_touched > 5 OR total_rows > 100000 | sort - total_rows
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 6 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same

references:

author: Clankerusecase

            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

Unpatched Ivanti Sentry appliances exposed to CVE-2026-10520 AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt that surfaces hosts still running pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1 Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) with CVE-2026-10520 (and the related CVE-2026-10523) still unpatched. Shadowserver reports widespread compromise of any unpatched Sentry that is internet-reachable, so this is the patch-status hunt that should run before the C2 hunt below. Rationale: Anchored on the exact CVE IDs from the article (CVE-2026-10520 + the sibling CVE-2026-10523 the BleepingComputer piece reuses) and the fixed-version strings Ivanti published (R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1). Cross-checked with Shadowserver's stat that ~all internet-exposed Sentry instances are likely backdoored, so IsInternetFacing is the priority pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.shadowserver.org/ • https://forums.ivanti.com/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-10520
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VM scanner snapshot lagging behind a freshly-patched Sentry node (status still reads vulnerable for ~24h)
  • Decommissioned Sentry VM still in CMDB but powered off and unreachable
  • Test/lab Sentry instance intentionally kept on R10.4.x for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Sentry behind an internal-only VIP showing as 'IsInternetFacing=false' but flagged anyway
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "R10.5.2" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "R10.6.2" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "R10.7.1"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SoftwareVersion column shows a build below R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 — Ivanti backported the fix into all three trains. Cross-check IsInternetFacing/PublicIP against external attack-surface scans. 2) Contain: ACL the Sentry admin VIP to corporate IPs only and force-upgrade. If the appliance was internet-reachable for >24h after CVE disclosure, treat as compromised per Shadowserver guidance — pull config, rotate any AD bind/service creds, force-reissue device certificates. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC #2 (anomalous outbound) on each vulnerable hostId, and dump /var/log on the Sentry filesystem for backdoor implants or new SUID binaries written since the disclosure date.

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc

Anomalous outbound connection from Ivanti Sentry appliance (CVE-2026-10520 backdoor) AICommand & Control High
Sentry appliances are management gateways; their outbound traffic profile is narrow (Ivanti cloud, NTP, DNS, syslog forwarder, MDM back-end). Shadowserver reports the CVE-2026-10520 PoC is being used to drop backdoors on most internet-exposed Sentry boxes — so any Sentry initiating a connection to a non-allowlisted public IP, especially on a non-standard port, is a strong post-exploitation indicator. Rationale: Pivot is the article's own framing: Shadowserver observed Sentry boxes being backdoored at scale via the public PoC for CVE-2026-10520, but the article gives no IOC hashes or specific C2 domains — so the highest-fidelity signal is a behavioural one (Sentry initiating outbound to non-allowlisted public IP/port). Allowed-ports set covers the standard Sentry egress (Ivanti telemetry, NTP, syslog, MDM HTTPS, admin HTTPS). Cross-checked against: • https://www.shadowserver.org/ • https://forums.ivanti.com/community/security-advisories
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Newly-onboarded Sentry pulling firmware/AV updates from a CDN edge IP on port 8080
  • Sentry forwarding telemetry to a SaaS log aggregator (Datadog/Sumo) on a non-standard port
  • Operator opening an outbound support tunnel to Ivanti TSE on a temporary port
  • Sentry reaching out to an externally-hosted CA/OCSP responder on port 80/443 (filtered, but URL-list edge cases)
  • MDM back-end reachable only via SaaS over port 8081 in some Sentry topologies
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteIP in ("<ivanti-cloud-cidrs>","<your-mdm-saas-ip>") or RemoteUrl has_any ("ivanti.com","mobileiron.com","<sanctioned-log-saas-domain>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm DeviceName is actually a Sentry appliance (not a host with 'sentry' in its hostname). Resolve the destination IP — is it Ivanti-owned, a known SaaS partner, or unattributed/VPS? Pull the same Sentry's syslog around the connect time for /mics or /authservice HTTP POSTs preceding the egress. 2) Contain: drop the Sentry's outbound at the perimeter (deny rule on DestinationIP), snapshot the appliance, and isolate from the corporate VLAN. 3) Hunt: across all Sentry boxes, summarize unique RemoteIP+RemotePort destinations over 30d — anything matching the new IP is the same backdoor. Also check for new files in /tmp, new cron entries, and new SSH authorized_keys on the appliance; rotate any AD bind, certificate, and API tokens the Sentry holds.
let SentryDevices = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where Vendor has "Ivanti" or DeviceName has "sentry" or DeviceName has "mobileiron" or OSDistribution has "sentry"
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
let AllowedPorts = dynamic([53, 80, 123, 443, 514, 8443]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (SentryDevices)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort !in (AllowedPorts)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Count=count(), SampleProcess=any(InitiatingProcessFileName), SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
let SentryHosts = Heartbeat
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where Computer has "sentry" or Computer has "mobileiron"
    | distinct Computer;
let AllowedPorts = dynamic([53, 80, 123, 443, 514, 8443]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SourceHostName in (SentryHosts) or SourceUserName in (SentryHosts)
| where DeviceAction in~ ("allow","accept","permit")
| where DestinationPort !in (AllowedPorts)
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == false
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Count=count() by SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:linux.syslog OR source:windows.sysmon) (@host:(*sentry* OR *SENTRY* OR *Sentry* OR *mobileiron* OR *MobileIron*)) -CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 192.168.0.0/16) -@network.destination.port:(53 OR 80 OR 123 OR 443 OR 514 OR 8443)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ComputerName=/sentry|mobileiron/i
| RemotePort!=53 RemotePort!=80 RemotePort!=123 RemotePort!=443 RemotePort!=514 RemotePort!=8443
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
| _count > 0

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.
