Langflow CVE-2026-5027 path-traversal POST to /api/v2/files AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POST requests to Langflow's vulnerable /api/v2/files endpoint carrying path-traversal markers in the URL/query or originating from non-browser scanner user-agents. Targets the active exploitation pattern reported by VulnCheck honeypots. Rationale: Targets the exact vulnerable endpoint (/api/v2/files) and HTTP verb (POST) named in Tenable's advisory and the article. Adds URL-encoded traversal variants (%2e%2e%2f / %252e%252e%252f) plus scanner user-agents commonly observed in VulnCheck honeypot exploitation. Defender query is intentionally narrow (port + Langflow process) since EDR cannot inspect HTTP bodies.
ATT&CKT1190 T1083
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing Langflow as part of authorised scans
  • CI/CD pipelines using curl or python-requests to upload flow definitions to a corporate Langflow instance
  • Legitimate ML engineers using the Langflow Python SDK (UA includes 'python-requests') against authorised internal hosts
  • Security research traffic from the org's own bug-bounty or red-team scope
  • Langflow's own integration tests run from the host's own subnet
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — suppress known scanners and CI/CD pipelines once allow-listed:
// | where SrcIP !in ("<corp_scanner_subnet>") and UA !contains "<corp_ci_agent_signature>"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the full POST body from WAF/proxy (if body logging is enabled) and confirm the multipart 'filename' field contains '../'. Check the response status — 200/201 means the write likely succeeded. Verify the Langflow instance version: anything pre-1.9.0 (or langflow-base pre-0.8.3) is vulnerable. Step 2 — Contain: Block the source IP at the WAF/edge. Take the Langflow instance offline if it's externally exposed and unpatched; restrict the listener to localhost or a VPN. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot to UC3 (Langflow file writes) on the same host within ±5 min of the POST; check /etc/cron*, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, /var/www/, /etc/ld.so.preload for new entries; review outbound connections from the python/uvicorn process for reverse-shell beacons; cross-check the source IP against MuddyWater infra given the prior CVE-2025-3248 linkage.
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no HTTP request-body visibility; this UC primarily targets W3C/WAF logs (see sentinel_kql). The closest Defender pivot is inbound network connections to the Langflow listener on the host.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort in (7860, 3000, 8000, 8080)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "uvicorn", "gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow", "langflow_base", "langflow.main")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize ConnCount=count(), Sources=make_set(RemoteIP, 50), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LocalPort
| where ConnCount > 5
| order by ConnCount desc
// Covers IIS/AppService and WAF/reverse-proxy via CommonSecurityLog
let traversal_re = @"(?i)(\.\./|%2e%2e%2f|%252e%252e%252f|\.\.%5c|\.\.\\\\)";
let scanner_ua_re = @"(?i)(curl|python-requests|go-http-client|nuclei|nmap|wget|httpx|fuzz|gobuster)";
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem has "/api/v2/files"
  | extend SrcIP=cIP, URL=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus), Source="IIS")
| union
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestURL has "/api/v2/files" or Message has "/api/v2/files"
  | extend SrcIP=SourceIP, URL=RequestURL, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct))
| union
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where CsUriStem has "/api/v2/files"
  | extend SrcIP=CIp, URL=strcat(CsUriStem,"?",CsUriQuery), UA=UserAgent, Status=tostring(ScStatus), Source="AppService")
| extend TraversalMarker = iff(URL matches regex traversal_re, true, false)
| extend ScannerUA = iff(UA matches regex scanner_ua_re, true, false)
| where TraversalMarker == true or ScannerUA == true or Status startswith "2"
| summarize Hits=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), URLs=make_set(URL, 10), UAs=make_set(UA, 10), Statuses=make_set(Status, 10), Markers=make_set(pack("traversal",TraversalMarker,"scanner_ua",ScannerUA),5) by SrcIP, Source
| order by Hits desc
title: Langflow CVE-2026-5027 Path Traversal POST to /api/v2/files
id: 8c4d2f01-9e1a-4b6f-9b8a-langflow5027a
status: experimental
description: Detects POST requests to Langflow's /api/v2/files endpoint with path-traversal markers or scanner user-agents, indicating exploitation of CVE-2026-5027.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/path-traversal-flaw-in-ai-dev-platform-langflow-exploited-in-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_endpoint:
    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/api/v2/files'
  selection_traversal:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '../'
      - '..%2f'
      - '%2e%2e%2f'
      - '%252e%252e'
      - '..%5c'
  selection_scanner_ua:
    c-useragent|contains:
      - 'curl/'
      - 'python-requests'
      - 'Go-http-client'
      - 'nuclei'
      - 'wget/'
      - 'httpx'
  condition: selection_endpoint and (selection_traversal or selection_scanner_ua)
falsepositives:
  - Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Nessus) probing the endpoint
  - Legitimate CI/CD pipelines uploading flow files via Langflow API
level: high
source:(nginx OR apache OR aws.alb OR azure.frontdoor OR cloudflare) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*\/api\/v2\/files* (@http.url:(*..%2F* OR *..%2f* OR *%2e%2e%2f* OR *..\/* ) OR @http.useragent:(*curl* OR *python-requests* OR *Go-http-client* OR *nuclei* OR *wget* OR *httpx*))
// Falcon EDR has no HTTP body inspection — this approximates by surfacing the Langflow listener accepting public connections; pair with proxy/WAF telemetry for body-level traversal markers.
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=1
| LocalPort=/^(7860|3000|8000|8080)$/
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(python|uvicorn|gunicorn)/i CommandLine=/langflow/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], key=[aid, TargetProcessId], include=[ImageFileName, CommandLine])
| regex("^(?!(10\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|192\\.168\\.))", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, LocalPort], function=[count(as=hits), count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=unique_src_ips)])
| hits > 5
# log group: /aws/applicationloadbalancer (point at the ALB fronting Langflow; for CloudFront use /aws/cloudfront)
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, user_agent, elb_status_code, target_status_code
| filter request_verb = "POST"
      and request_url like /\/api\/v2\/files/
      and (request_url like /\.\.\// or request_url like /%2e%2e%2f/i or user_agent like /(curl|python-requests|Go-http-client|nuclei|wget|httpx)/i)
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200

Langflow auto-login token issuance followed by /api/v2/files POST within seconds AIExploitation High
Detects the credential_access pattern unique to CVE-2026-5027 exploitation: an external IP hits Langflow's unauthenticated auto-login endpoint to mint a session token, then immediately POSTs to /api/v2/files. This single-IP burst pattern is the lowest-effort exploit signature and is the shape VulnCheck honeypots describe. Rationale: Captures the exploit kill chain the VulnCheck post describes — a single unauthenticated session-token mint immediately followed by the file upload. The 30-second window matches scripted exploit cadence; legitimate users take longer between login and first action. Article quote: 'a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token before proceeding with exploitation'.
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1539 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Langflow users behind a shared NAT egressing from one corporate IP — login then immediate API usage
  • Automated CI/CD pipelines calling auto_login then file upload as part of nightly flow-deployment jobs
  • Vulnerability scanners that intentionally script the login+endpoint sequence to test reachability
  • Selenium / Playwright smoke tests against staging Langflow that mimic this exact pattern
  • Langflow's own integration test suite hitting localhost
Suppression filter
// Suppress known internal CI ranges (Sentinel): | where SrcIP !in ("<corp_ci_egress_ip_1>","<corp_ci_egress_ip_2>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the source IP is external/untrusted and not on the corporate egress list. Pull the full request chain — was the login a 200 with a new session cookie? Was the file POST a 200/201 (write succeeded) or 400 (rejected)? Step 2 — Contain: Block the IP at the WAF, force-rotate any Langflow session signing keys, and patch the instance to 1.10.0 immediately (1.9.0 also fixes 5027 but 1.10.0 is the latest as of the article). Disable auto-login by setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false. Step 3 — Hunt: Look for the same SrcIP in the prior 30 days to spot reconnaissance; correlate with UC3 (file writes by python/uvicorn outside upload dir) on the host hosting Langflow within 60s of the upload event.
// Defender Advanced Hunting cannot see HTTP request paths; the correlation lives at the proxy/WAF layer. See sentinel_kql.
let lookback = 7d;
let window = 30s;
let WebReqs = union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | extend SrcIP=cIP, URL=csUriStem, Method=csMethod, Status=tostring(scStatus), Source="IIS"),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | extend SrcIP=SourceIP, URL=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), Source=DeviceProduct),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | extend SrcIP=CIp, URL=CsUriStem, Method=CsMethod, Status=tostring(ScStatus), Source="AppService")
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIP, URL, Method, Status, Source;
let Logins = WebReqs | where URL has_any ("/api/v1/auto_login", "/api/v1/login") | project LoginTime=TimeGenerated, SrcIP, LoginURL=URL, LoginStatus=Status, Source;
let Uploads = WebReqs | where URL has "/api/v2/files" and Method =~ "POST" | project UploadTime=TimeGenerated, SrcIP, UploadURL=URL, UploadStatus=Status;
Logins
| join kind=inner Uploads on SrcIP
| where UploadTime between (LoginTime .. LoginTime + window)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', UploadTime, LoginTime)
| summarize Pairs=count(), FirstLogin=min(LoginTime), FirstUpload=min(UploadTime), MinDelay=min(DelaySec), URLs=make_set(UploadURL, 5) by SrcIP, Source
| where Pairs >= 1
| order by MinDelay asc
source:(nginx OR apache OR aws.alb OR azure.frontdoor OR cloudflare) (@http.url_details.path:*\/api\/v1\/auto_login* OR (@http.method:POST AND @http.url_details.path:*\/api\/v2\/files*))
# log group: /aws/applicationloadbalancer (point at the ALB fronting Langflow)
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, elb_status_code
| filter request_url like /\/api\/v1\/auto_login/ or (request_verb = "POST" and request_url like /\/api\/v2\/files/)
| stats count(*) as hits, earliest(@timestamp) as first_hit, latest(@timestamp) as last_hit, count_distinct(request_url) as distinct_urls by client_ip, bin(1m)
| filter distinct_urls >= 2 and hits >= 2
| sort first_hit desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*api/v1/auto_login*" OR Web.url="*api/v1/login*" OR (Web.url="*api/v2/files*" AND Web.http_method=POST)) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.status _time
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| where action!="other"
| sort 0 src _time
| streamstats window=2 values(action) as actions values(_time) as times values(url) as urls values(status) as statuses by src dest
| where mvcount(actions)=2 AND mvindex(actions,0)="login" AND mvindex(actions,1)="upload"

Langflow python/uvicorn process writing files outside expected data directory AIInstallation High
Detects the post-exploitation file-write side-effect of CVE-2026-5027: the Langflow service (python / uvicorn / gunicorn running 'langflow') drops files into directories outside its normal upload/data path — particularly into cron, SSH key, web-root, library-preload, or systemd unit paths. Matches the VulnCheck-reported behaviour of attackers dropping marker/test files via path traversal. Rationale: Pivots on the exact process Langflow runs as (python/uvicorn/gunicorn with 'langflow' in cmdline) and the file-write side-effect named in the kill chain: 'Watch for the Langflow process (python/uvicorn) writing files to paths outside its expected upload/data directories, especially into /etc, /root, cron paths, or web roots.' Explicitly filters out the legitimate Langflow data directory to keep precision high.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1565.001 T1098.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow first-run setup writing default config to /root/.langflow/ if running as root (filtered)
  • Custom Langflow components that legitimately export artefacts to /usr/local/share or /tmp
  • pip install run inside the Langflow venv writing console_scripts shims into /usr/local/bin
  • Container image build writing layers to /etc/profile.d (build-time, not runtime — distinguish via process ancestry)
  • Admin SSH'd into the host running ad-hoc python scripts named 'langflow_something.py' that legitimately touch system paths
Suppression filter
// Tighten by requiring the file write to be NEW (not modification of an existing file the process legitimately owns):
// Defender: | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
// Sentinel ImFileEvent: | where EventType == "FileCreated"
// And exclude package-install paths if Langflow pip-installs at runtime:
// | where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("pip", "pip3", "poetry", "uv"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Read the written file's contents immediately (cat) and SHA-256 hash it; check if it's a webshell, a cron entry calling out, an SSH key for an unknown user, or an ld.so.preload library. Pull the parent /api/v2/files POST from web logs to confirm the path-traversal sequence. Step 2 — Contain: Stop the Langflow service (systemctl stop langflow), quarantine the host network connectivity, snapshot the disk for forensics. Remove the dropped file ONLY after capturing it. Step 3 — Hunt: List all files written by the Langflow process in the prior 30 days outside the data dir; review crontab and systemd unit listings; check authorized_keys across all users; review outbound network connections from python/uvicorn for C2; cross-check the source IP from the triggering POST against threat intel (especially MuddyWater infra per CVE-2025-3248 linkage). Patch to Langflow 1.10.0 before bringing the host back online.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "python3.10", "python3.11", "python3.12", "uvicorn", "gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow", "langflow_base", "langflow.main", "langflow.__main__")
| extend PathLower = tolower(FolderPath)
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron"
    or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron"
    or (FolderPath has ".ssh" and FileName =~ "authorized_keys")
    or FullPath =~ "/etc/ld.so.preload"
    or (FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system" and FileName endswith ".service")
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/profile.d"

Miasma dead-man-switch destructive home directory wipe AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the exact destructive payload the Miasma monitor executes when the stolen GitHub token is revoked: a chained `rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`. This is the worm's burn-down trigger, fires on Linux and macOS developer hosts. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim destructive command in code block [1] of the article (`rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`). The two-tier rm chain on `~` plus `~/Documents` in a single command line is a fingerprint of the dead-man switch — legitimate cleanup never deletes the entire home and then re-deletes Documents. Corroborated with SafeDep and Cloudsmith write-ups of the same dead-man-switch logic in the dropped systemd/LaunchAgent monitor. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-worm-hits-73-microsoft-github.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer factory-resetting a personal VM with a bootstrap script that wipes home before re-cloning dotfiles
  • Test-harness teardown on a CI sandbox host that destroys the runner's home directory
  • An IR/forensics analyst executing a documented host-wipe runbook prior to re-imaging
  • A frustrated dev running the command interactively as a joke after a bad merge
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("image-builder","packer","cloud-init")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/var/lib/cloud"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !contains "vm-rebuild"
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the originating process tree — the parent should be the Miasma monitor (`systemd --user` service or `launchd` LaunchAgent) launched within the last 72 hours; correlate the AccountName with recent api.github.com PAT activity. Contain: Immediately freeze the user's GitHub PAT (the revocation IS the trigger — but the destruction is already running, so isolate the host from network and snapshot disk before the worm finishes recursing). Hunt: across the fleet for sibling systemd user services or LaunchAgents created in the same window referencing api.github.com token-validity polling; pivot on the user's GitHub identity to find other developer hosts where the same PAT was used.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rm -rf" and ProcessCommandLine has "Documents"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~|\$HOME)/?\s*(;|&&|\||\n)"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~|\$HOME)/Documents"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs in~ ("Linux","macOS","Darwin")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "rm -rf" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Documents"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~|\$HOME)/?\s*(;|&&|\|)"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~|\$HOME)/Documents"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm Dead-Man-Switch Home Directory Wipe
id: 7b1e9f2a-3a8c-4d10-9c5d-3bd7d6c0f211
description: Detects the exact destructive chained rm -rf command Miasma executes when its stolen GitHub PAT is revoked (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents). Triggered by the systemd user service or LaunchAgent monitor installed by the worm.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/
  - https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/

author: SOC Detection Engineering

  condition: selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Factory-reset scripts run on freshly-imaged developer VMs
  - Sandbox teardown automation
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*"rm -rf ~/"* OR *"rm -rf $HOME/"*) AND @process.command_line:(*"rm -rf ~/Documents"* OR *"rm -rf $HOME/Documents"*)) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/lib/snapd/* OR /var/lib/cloud/instance/scripts/*)
#event_simpleName=/^(Synthetic)?ProcessRollup2$/
| regex("(?i)rm\\s+-rf\\s+(~|\\$HOME)/?\\s*(;|&&|\\|)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)rm\\s+-rf\\s+(~|\\$HOME)/Documents", field=CommandLine)

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Miasma 72-hour monitor persistence via systemd user service or LaunchAgent AIInstallation High
Hunts the Miasma persistence dropper — a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent plist on macOS, written by a non-package-manager process, that subsequently beacons to api.github.com. The article specifies this monitor polls GitHub-token validity every minute for up to 72 hours. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit statement that the Miasma monitor `runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS, and remains active for up to 72 hours`. The token-validity poll runs every minute, so a fresh persistence drop chained to >=20 api.github.com beacons within 72h is an extremely tight fingerprint. SHA256 IOCs from the campaign embedded as confirmation tier. Corroborated against SafeDep's analysis and Cloudsmith's persistence-chain write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-worm-hits-73-microsoft-github.html
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1543.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Homebrew installing a user LaunchAgent (e.g. `homebrew.mxcl.<svc>.plist`) — likely beaconing for tap updates
  • VS Code Remote / Cursor Remote tunnel installing a per-user systemd service that calls api.github.com for tunnel registration
  • fnm / nvm / Volta installing a LaunchAgent shell hook
  • Dotfile-bootstrap script (chezmoi/yadm) deploying personal LaunchAgents from a developer's repo
  • gh CLI auth refresh polling api.github.com on a host with a legit pre-existing service
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("brew","installer","Code Helper","Cursor Helper","node-gyp","fnm","nvm","volta","chezmoi","yadm")
| where not (TargetFilePath has "homebrew.mxcl." or TargetFilePath has "com.microsoft.VSCode" or TargetFilePath has "com.cursor.")
Response runbook
Triage: Read the unit/plist contents (`cat`) and verify the ExecStart command — Miasma units shell out to `node` or `python` with an embedded one-liner that reads a stored GitHub PAT and HEADs api.github.com. Validate the InitiatingProcessFileName — legit drops come from `brew`, `installer`, `Code Helper`; Miasma drops come from `node`, `npm`, `python`, `bash`, `git`. Contain: Stop the service (`systemctl --user stop`/`launchctl bootout`), pull the unit file for IR, revoke any GitHub PATs scoped to that user — BUT first capture the host disk image, because revocation triggers the dead-man switch detection (UC1). Hunt: cross-reference InitiatingProcessSHA256 fleet-wide; pivot the user's GitHub identity through audit log to identify packages/repos pushed in the persistence window.
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic(["396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4","d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223","f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c","d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b","f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f","25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b","d630397de8b01af0f6f5cf4463da91b17f28195a2c50c8f3f38ad9f7873fdb8e","3a9db5ba0c8cd4c91e91717df6b1a141fc1e0fbc0558b5a78d7f5c23f5b2a150"]);
let PersistenceDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/\.config/systemd/user(/|$)"
          or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/Library/LaunchAgents(/|$)"
          or FileName endswith ".service" and FolderPath has "systemd/user"
          or FileName endswith ".plist" and FolderPath has "LaunchAgents"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("systemd","launchd","brew","apt","apt-get","dpkg","yum","dnf","snap","installer","pkg","Code","Code Helper","Cursor","Cursor Helper")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId;
let GithubBeacons = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","github.com")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessId;
PersistenceDrops
| join kind=inner GithubBeacons on DeviceName
| where NetTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 72h)
| summarize BeaconCount = count(), FirstBeacon = min(NetTime), LastBeacon = max(NetTime)
          by Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where BeaconCount >= 20
| extend KnownHash = SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
| order by Timestamp desc
let PersistenceDrops = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/\.config/systemd/user/.*\.service$"
          or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/Library/LaunchAgents/.*\.plist$"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("systemd","launchd","brew","apt","dpkg","yum","dnf","snap","installer","pkg","Code","Cursor")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let GithubBeacons = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("api.github.com","github.com")
    | project BeaconTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstHostname, DstIpAddr;
PersistenceDrops
| join kind=inner GithubBeacons on DvcHostname
| where BeaconTime between (DropTime .. DropTime + 72h)
| summarize BeaconCount = count() by DropTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where BeaconCount >= 20
| order by DropTime desc

      - '/launchd'
      - '/brew'
      - '/apt'
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/snap'
      - '/installer'
      - '/Code'
      - '/Cursor'
  condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Homebrew services installing user-level LaunchAgents
  - VS Code Server / Cursor Server installing remote-tunnel systemd units
  - fnm/nvm install scripts dropping LaunchAgents for shell hooks
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @auditd.type:PATH (@file.path:*"/.config/systemd/user/"*.service OR @file.path:*"/Library/LaunchAgents/"*.plist) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/lib/systemd/* OR /usr/bin/brew OR /usr/local/bin/brew OR /usr/bin/apt OR /usr/bin/apt-get OR /usr/bin/dpkg OR /usr/sbin/installer OR */Code OR */Cursor)

| NOT regex("(?i)(/systemd$|/launchd$|/brew$|/apt$|/dpkg$|/installer$|/snap$|/Code$|/Cursor$)", field=ContextImageFileName)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\\.)github\\.com$/i}, field=aid, key=GithubCallbackAid, include=[ComputerName, DomainName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())

Miasma AI coding tool config poisoning via non-IDE writer AIInstallation Medium
Hunts writes to AI-coding-assistant config directories (~/.claude, ~/.cursor, ~/.gemini, ~/.config/github-copilot, ~/.kiro, ~/.cline) performed by a shell, package manager, or scripting runtime rather than the IDE/agent binary itself. The article calls out Miasma poisoning these exact tools to weaponize the next developer prompt. Rationale: The article explicitly names `Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline` as the AI tools whose configs Miasma poisons. The detection is the WRITE side: the IDE/agent binary normally owns its config dir, so a shell/npm/git/python writing into `~/.claude` or `~/.cursor` is the worm planting the prompt-injection payload. Corroborated by SafeDep's `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` repo analysis which confirms the config-injection vector. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://complexdiscovery.com/when-the-worm-targets-the-assistant-miasma-turns-ai-coding-agents-into-the-trigger/
ATT&CKT1546 T1059 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • chezmoi / yadm dotfile-sync writing `~/.cursor/settings.json` from a developer's tracked repo
  • Manual `cp` or `echo > ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` while the developer is hand-editing memory rules
  • npm-installed VS Code extension postinstall script writing to `~/.config/github-copilot/`
  • Cursor / Claude Code self-update routed through a `curl | sh` installer (writes happen as `bash`)
  • Developer pasting a config bootstrap from documentation that uses `cat <<EOF > ~/.kiro/config.yaml`
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("chezmoi","yadm","stow","dotbot")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "update" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","cursor","gemini","copilot","kiro","cline"))
Response runbook
Triage: Diff the written file against the previous version in source control (most devs version their AI configs) — look for added shell commands, `curl|sh` patterns, or MCP server registrations pointing to suspicious npm/GitHub URLs. Inspect the writing process tree: a `node` parent that just ran `npm install <pkg>` is the supply-chain pivot. Contain: Revert the config file from the last-known-good git commit, kill any agent/MCP processes the poisoned config started, isolate the host if MCP execution already fired. Hunt: across the org for the same file SHA256 — Miasma uses a per-build payload but the injected MCP/agent definition often reuses domain or repo strings; pivot on those.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/\.(claude|cursor|gemini|kiro|cline)(/|$)"
      or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/\.config/(github-copilot|copilot|cursor|kiro|cline)(/|$)"
      or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/Library/Application Support/(Claude|Cursor|GitHub Copilot|Gemini|Kiro|Cline)/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh","dash","node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","python","python3","git","curl","wget","ruby","gem","pip","pip3","tar","unzip")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("claude","cursor","Cursor Helper","Code","Code Helper","gemini","copilot","kiro","cline")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName endswith ".md" or FileName endswith ".json" or FileName endswith ".yaml" or FileName endswith ".yml" or FileName endswith ".toml" or FileName startswith "AGENTS" or FileName startswith "CLAUDE" or FileName has "mcp" or FileName has "settings"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/\.(claude|cursor|gemini|kiro|cline)(/|$)"
      or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/\.config/(github-copilot|copilot|cursor|kiro|cline)(/|$)"
      or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)/Library/Application Support/(Claude|Cursor|GitHub Copilot|Gemini|Kiro|Cline)/"
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh","dash","node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","python","python3","git","curl","wget","ruby","gem","pip","pip3","tar","unzip")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("claude","cursor","Code","Code Helper","gemini","copilot","kiro","cline")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".md" or TargetFileName endswith ".json" or TargetFileName endswith ".yaml" or TargetFileName endswith ".yml" or TargetFileName has_any ("AGENTS","CLAUDE","mcp","settings")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma AI Coding Agent Config Poisoning by Non-IDE Process

description: Detects writes to AI coding assistant config directories (Claude, Cursor, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, Cline) by shells, package managers, scripting runtimes, or git — i.e. anything that is not the IDE/agent binary itself. Miasma uses this to plant instructions the next prompt will execute, turning the AI assistant into a trigger for the credential-stealer.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/
  - https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/

| regex("(?i)/(bash|sh|zsh|dash|node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|python|python3|git|curl|wget|ruby|gem|pip|pip3|tar|unzip)$", field=ContextImageFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)/(claude|cursor|Code|Code Helper|gemini|copilot|kiro|cline)$", field=ContextImageFileName)

Miasma developer credential file harvest fan-out AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts a single non-allowlisted process reading four or more distinct developer credential / secret-store files within a one-minute window. The article describes Miasma harvesting cloud provider, CI/CD, password manager, Kubernetes, and secret-store credentials in one stage; this aggregates that across the canonical dotfile locations. Rationale: The article enumerates the categories Miasma harvests — `cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores` — which maps to the canonical Unix dotfile locations (.aws, .npmrc, .pypirc, .gem, .kube, .docker, .config/gh, .ssh, .config/op, .password-store, .jfrog). A single unknown process touching 4+ of these inside 60s is the fan-out shape. Sigma is intentionally omitted because the detection is a count-threshold over a time bin, which Sigma's single-event-shape doesn't express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A Time Machine / restic / borg backup sweeping the user's home directory
  • A dev running `env | grep` after sourcing a project's `direnv` that pulls AWS+kube+npm creds in sequence (likely caught by allowlist)
  • A new-machine bootstrap script copying dotfiles from a USB stick
  • An IR/forensics agent (Velociraptor, GRR) running a credential-inventory hunt
  • Cloud-config sync tooling (e.g. `aws-vault sync`, `kubelogin`)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tmutil","rsync","restic","borg","kopia","velociraptor","osqueryd","aws-vault","kubelogin","direnv")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "backup" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "snapshot")
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the offending process's full image path and SHA256, and check if it's a Node/Python/Bash one-liner forked from npm/pip install. Cross-reference `InitiatingProcessParentFileName` — Miasma typically arrives as `node` under `npm`/`npx` (the postinstall hook), so a `node` parent of `npm install` is high-confidence. Contain: Force-rotate every credential the process touched — AWS access keys, npm/pypi/rubygems tokens, JFrog API keys, GitHub PATs, kubeconfig contexts. Disable the user's CI/CD pipelines until reviewed. Hunt: pivot the GitHub PAT to find any new repos created under that account (Miasma exfils to dead-drop repos under accounts like `liuende501`, `windy629`, `HerGomUli`); list packages published by the user across npm/PyPI/RubyGems in the last 24h.
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([
    "/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.npmrc","/.pypirc",
    "/.gem/credentials","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json",
    "/.netrc","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/git/credentials",
    "/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa",
    "/.config/op/","/.password-store/","/.cargo/credentials","/.jfrog/"
]);
let AllowedReaders = dynamic([
    "aws","kubectl","docker","ssh","sshd","git","gh","node","npm","pnpm","yarn",
    "gem","pip","pip3","gpg","op","1password","Code","Code Helper","Cursor",
    "claude","tmutil","rsync","restic","borg","kopia"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileOpened","FileRead","FileCreated")
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FullPath has_any (CredPathFragments)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (AllowedReaders)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize CredsHit = dcount(FullPath), SamplePaths = make_set(FullPath, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
             InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
             bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where CredsHit >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([
    "/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.npmrc","/.pypirc",
    "/.gem/credentials","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json",
    "/.netrc","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/git/credentials",
    "/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa",
    "/.config/op/","/.password-store/","/.cargo/credentials","/.jfrog/"
]);
let AllowedReaders = dynamic([
    "aws","kubectl","docker","ssh","sshd","git","gh","node","npm","pnpm","yarn",
    "gem","pip","pip3","gpg","op","Code","Cursor","claude","tmutil","rsync",
    "restic","borg","kopia"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened","FileCreated")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathFragments)
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (AllowedReaders)
| summarize CredsHit = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
             ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where CredsHit >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH (@file.path:*/.aws/credentials OR @file.path:*/.aws/config OR @file.path:*/.npmrc OR @file.path:*/.pypirc OR @file.path:*/.gem/credentials OR @file.path:*/.kube/config OR @file.path:*/.docker/config.json OR @file.path:*/.netrc OR @file.path:*/.config/gh/hosts.yml OR @file.path:*/.config/git/credentials OR @file.path:*/.ssh/id_rsa OR @file.path:*/.ssh/id_ed25519 OR @file.path:*/.ssh/id_ecdsa OR @file.path:*/.config/op/* OR @file.path:*/.password-store/* OR @file.path:*/.cargo/credentials* OR @file.path:*/.jfrog/*) -@process.name:(aws OR kubectl OR docker OR ssh OR sshd OR git OR gh OR node OR npm OR yarn OR pnpm OR gem OR pip OR pip3 OR gpg OR op OR tmutil OR rsync OR restic OR borg OR kopia)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo
| regex("(?i)(/\\.aws/credentials|/\\.aws/config|/\\.npmrc|/\\.pypirc|/\\.gem/credentials|/\\.kube/config|/\\.docker/config\\.json|/\\.netrc|/\\.config/gh/hosts\\.yml|/\\.config/git/credentials|/\\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|/\\.config/op/|/\\.password-store/|/\\.cargo/credentials|/\\.jfrog/)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)/(aws|kubectl|docker|ssh|sshd|git|gh|node|npm|yarn|pnpm|gem|pip|pip3|gpg|op|Code|Cursor|claude|tmutil|rsync|restic|borg|kopia)$", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), as=CredsHit)
| CredsHit>=4

| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_path) as cred_paths_hit, values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths_sampled, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.pypirc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gem/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.netrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/git/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ed25519" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ecdsa" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/op/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.password-store/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cargo/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.jfrog/*") Filesystem.action IN (read, accessed, opened) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where cred_paths_hit >= 4 | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)^(aws|kubectl|docker|ssh|sshd|git|gh|node|npm|pnpm|yarn|gem|pip|pip3|gpg|op|1password|Code|Cursor|claude|TimeMachine|tmutil|rsync|restic|borg|kopia)$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Miasma-Open-Source-Release repository fetch via git clone or HTTP download AIDelivery High
Hunts any process referencing the exact GitHub repository name `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` — the repo name SafeDep observed the threat actors using across compromised developer accounts to publish the leaked source. Covers `git clone`, `curl`/`wget` of the tarball, and browser-mediated downloads. Rationale: `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` is the exact repository naming convention SafeDep observed across every compromised developer account distributing the leaked toolkit (article: `the threat actors leaked the source code in a repo named "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"`). The string is unique enough that any process or HTTP reference is high-fidelity. Corroborated by SafeDep, The Register, and Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-worm-hits-73-microsoft-github.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC / IR analyst pulling the repo for forensic analysis
  • Threat-intel team automatically ingesting the artefact via gh CLI
  • Security researcher mirroring the repo to a private archive
  • DFIR sandbox detonating the repo in a controlled environment
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("ir-sandbox-01","ti-ingest-01","malware-lab-01")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("cape","cuckoo","any.run")
Response runbook
Triage: Identify the requester — if it's a security analyst on the IR team running from a known forensic workstation, suppress and document. For any other host, treat it as suspected first-stage execution. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the host in a +/- 10-minute window to see what ran after the clone. Contain: Isolate the host from the network and quarantine the cloned directory. Preserve any GitHub credentials present on disk for IR. Hunt: Pivot the GitHub username portion of the URL (e.g. `github.com/<user>/Miasma-Open-Source-Release`) — that account is compromised; check if any internal developers have starred, forked, or have collaborator access. Search for sibling drop accounts (`liuende501`, `windy629`, `HerGomUli`) referenced across the fleet.
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EventKind = "process",
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName),
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          EventKind = "network", FileName = "", ProcessCommandLine = RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName = InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventKind = "process",
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "Miasma-Open-Source-Release"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername = SrcUsername,
          EventKind = "network", ActingProcessName = "", ActingProcessCommandLine = Url,
          ParentProcessName = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Reference to Miasma-Open-Source-Release Worm Source Repository
id: 1a5e8f97-d2bb-4c39-9e02-6fa14d8b3c44
description: Detects any process command line or HTTP request referencing the exact GitHub repository name `Miasma-Open-Source-Release` — the repo name SafeDep observed across compromised developer accounts publishing the leaked Miasma worm source code.

(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2)

AWS SSM cross-host fan-out from a developer IAM principal AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts AWS Systems Manager `StartSession`/`SendCommand`/`StartAutomationExecution` events from a single IAM user / assumed role hitting many distinct instance targets in a short window. The article calls out SSM as one of Miasma's two lateral movement primitives after harvesting cloud creds. Rationale: The article explicitly names `SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM)` as Miasma's lateral movement primitives. After stealing AWS keys from `~/.aws/credentials` (caught by UC4), the worm pivots into SSM to reach EC2 hosts and run commands. A single principal hitting 5+ distinct targets in 10 minutes is the spread shape. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon are intentionally empty because CloudTrail telemetry doesn't natively flow into those backends; CloudWatch and Datadog are the right destinations. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/12/09/shai-hulud-2-0-guidance-for-detecting-investigating-and-defending-against-the-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/k/shai-hulud-2-0-targets-cloud-and-developer-systems.html • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/
ATT&CKT1021.008 T1078.004 T1570
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager scheduled patching window
  • DevOps engineer running a fleet-wide configuration update via `aws ssm send-command --targets`
  • Automated drift remediation pipeline running from a CI/CD role
  • Incident response triage where on-call SRE pulls diagnostics from many hosts at once
  • Bulk RDP/SSH bootstrap via SSM for a newly-launched ASG
Suppression filter
| filter userIdentity.arn not like /role\/SSMPatchManager/
      and userIdentity.arn not like /role\/.*-cicd-/
      and not (requestParameters.documentName like /AWS-RunPatchBaseline|AWS-UpdateSSMAgent/)
      and additionalEventData.MFAUsed = "No"
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the IAM principal's recent AssumeRole / GetSessionToken events and check `additionalEventData.MFAUsed` — Miasma stole long-lived AWS keys, so the SSM calls won't have an MFA-backed session. Verify `sourceIPAddress` against the user's normal egress (developer IP vs unknown VPS). Contain: Revoke the access key (`UpdateAccessKey` to Inactive), kill all running SSM sessions for that principal (`TerminateSession`), rotate the IAM user's credentials, and put a deny policy on the role for `ssm:*` while investigating. Hunt: Enumerate every instance the principal touched (`requestParameters.target`/`instanceIds`) — those are now suspect-lateral; run the credential-harvest detection (UC4) on each. Check S3/ECR/Lambda actions from the same principal in the same window for staging activity.
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(StartSession OR SendCommand OR StartAutomationExecution) @evt.source:ssm.amazonaws.com @evt.outcome:success -@userIdentity.arn:(*"role/SSMPatchManager"* OR *"role/aws-service-role"* OR *"role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole"* OR *"role/AWSServiceRoleFor"*)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.attributes.mfaAuthenticated, requestParameters.target, requestParameters.instanceIds, requestParameters.documentName, awsRegion
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
     and eventName in ["StartSession","SendCommand","StartAutomationExecution"]
     and not isPresent(errorCode)
     and userIdentity.arn not like /aws-service-role|SSMPatchManager|OrganizationAccountAccessRole|AWSServiceRoleFor/
| stats count(*) as ssm_calls,
        count_distinct(requestParameters.target) as distinct_targets,
        earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen,
        latest(@timestamp) as last_seen,
        count_distinct(awsRegion) as regions_touched
        by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName
| filter distinct_targets >= 5
| sort last_seen desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(All_Changes.object) as target_count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(All_Changes.command) as actions, values(All_Changes.object) as targets from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.command IN ("StartSession","SendCommand","StartAutomationExecution") All_Changes.result="success" sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" by All_Changes.user All_Changes.src All_Changes.user_type _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where target_count >= 5 | where NOT match(user, "(?i)^(arn:aws:iam::\d+:role/(SSMPatchManager|aws-service-role|AWSServiceRoleFor|OrganizationAccountAccessRole|ssm-automation-))") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |

references:

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or SHA1 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or MD5 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or SHA1 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or MD5 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Defender TVM flags CVE-2026-48063 (vulnerable Baileys npm package) on host AIExploitation High
Surfaces hosts where Defender Threat & Vulnerability Management has identified the npm:baileys / npm:@whiskeysockets/baileys package at a vulnerable version (< 6.7.22 or 7.0.0-rc.1 ≤ x < 7.0.0-rc12). This is the cleanest, lowest-FP route to find exposed WhatsApp-bot/automation hosts before exploitation via a crafted protocolMessage payload. Rationale: Direct CVE pivot — the advisory itself supplies CVE-2026-48063 as the canonical identifier. TVM/SBOM-grounded detection is the lowest-FP shape for a pure library vulnerability with no host-side TTPs. No external corroboration needed; the GitHub Security Advisory IS the authoritative source.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1190
Data sourcesVulnerability_Management.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Stale TVM data shortly after a successful upgrade (next TVM scan will clear it)
  • Dev/test workstations where baileys is installed but never connected to a real WhatsApp session
  • TVM version-parsing miss-attributing a back-ported security fix in a forked baileys build
  • Container build images flagged but never deployed to runtime
  • Pre-release ≥7.0.0-rc12 incorrectly version-compared by the scanner
Suppression filter
| where VulnerabilitySeverityLevel in ("High","Critical")
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "7.0.0-rc12" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "7.0.0-rc.12"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm SoftwareVersion sits in the vulnerable range (< 6.7.22, or 7.0.0-rc.1 ≤ x < 7.0.0-rc12). Identify the package owner via repo, code-owner file, or LoggedOnUsers. Check if the host actually has a live WhatsApp session (look for sustained TCP to *.whatsapp.net / web.whatsapp.com from node.exe). 2) Contain: open a P2 patch ticket for owner to upgrade to 6.7.22 / 7.0.0-rc12. Workaround until patched — drop messages.upsert events containing a requestId field and set shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false in socket config. 3) Hunt: enumerate every other host with the file-event UC (paired UC2) to find shadow-IT baileys deployments TVM missed; pivot on parent node.exe command lines referencing automation scripts.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48063"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, LoggedOnUsers
| order by Timestamp desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48063"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, OSPlatform, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, LoggedOnUsers
| order by TimeGenerated desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Vulnerabilities.signature) as Signatures values(Vulnerabilities.severity) as Severity FROM datamodel=Vulnerabilities WHERE Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48063" BY Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - lastSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Vulnerabilities.signature) as Signatures values(Vulnerabilities.severity) as Severity FROM datamodel=Vulnerabilities WHERE Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48063" BY Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - lastSeen
Vulnerable Baileys npm package install/presence on Windows endpoints AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for file-write activity inside node_modules\baileys or node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys directories — surfaces hosts running the vulnerable WhatsApp library even when TVM/SBOM tooling has no signal on the npm package. Pair with UC1 (TVM) to cover environments without SBOM ingestion. Rationale: Uses the exact package paths from the advisory's affected-packages list (npm:baileys and npm:@whiskeysockets/baileys). File-path hunting catches shadow-IT installs that TVM/SBOM never enrolled. Cross-platform path variants (\ vs /) included for WSL/dev containers. Excludes Defender self-scan noise.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate corporate WhatsApp bot/automation projects running an already-patched baileys version (≥6.7.22 or ≥7.0.0-rc12)
  • Developer workstations where engineers clone open-source baileys for unrelated work
  • Jenkins/GitHub Actions self-hosted runners pulling baileys as a build-stage transitive dependency
  • Container build hosts producing baileys-containing images that are deployed elsewhere
  • Backup/restore agents replaying historical node_modules archives onto recovery hosts
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\AppData\Local\Temp\", "\Windows\Temp\") and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MsiExec.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the actual baileys version from the host's package.json (DeviceFileEvents won't tell you the version, only the path). If owner cannot be identified from the directory tree, use InitiatingProcessAccountName / LoggedOnUsers from DeviceInfo. 2) Contain: if vulnerable version (< 6.7.22 or 7.0.0-rc.1 ≤ x < 7.0.0-rc12), open a patch ticket and apply the workaround (drop messages.upsert events containing requestId, set shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false). For internet-facing bot hosts treat as priority. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName for outbound traffic to *.whatsapp.net / web.whatsapp.com from node.exe to confirm an active WhatsApp session is bound to the vulnerable lib; enumerate other repos in the same project group that may share the dependency.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\baileys\", @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\", "/node_modules/baileys/", "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(FileName, 25), Installers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\node_modules\baileys\", @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\", "/node_modules/baileys/", "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), FileCount = count(), SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFileName, 25), Installers = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Vulnerable Baileys npm package present on host (CVE-2026-48063)
id: 7f3a2d4e-5b6c-4d7a-9e8f-1c2b3a4d5e6f
description: Detects file-write activity inside node_modules\baileys or node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys, surfacing endpoints running the WhatsApp library vulnerable to message upsert / history sync spoofing via crafted protocolMessage payloads.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
  - https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\baileys\'
      - '\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\baileys\\* OR @TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\* OR @TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\@WhiskeySockets\\baileys\\*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\(baileys|@whiskeysockets\\\\baileys)\\\\", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|corepack)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Filesystem.file_name) as Files values(Filesystem.process_name) as InitiatingProcess FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem WHERE (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\baileys\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/baileys/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/*") BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - lastSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Filesystem.file_name) as Files values(Filesystem.process_name) as InitiatingProcess FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem WHERE (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\baileys\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/baileys/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/*") BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstSeen) ctime(lastSeen)
| sort - lastSeen
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48063")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48063")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48063")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48063")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
